<reason>B more convincingly distinguished useful clearance sales from a justified universal requirement. A established plausible recovery benefits, but did not resolve the meaningful-selling-window problem or justify compulsory attempts where recovery is unlikely. B answered its pressure questions directly and explained how disposal charges could encourage both recovery and prevention. A increasingly relied on calling disposal “Plan B” rather than showing why its procedure produced the better tradeoff.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s strongest response turned A’s “pay and keep wasting” objection back on the mandate: stores could also pay compliance labor and discard the same food afterward. B then explained that fees can induce the very markdowns A favors while additionally rewarding prevention. A’s distinction between attempted and unattempted disposal did not adequately answer that comparison.</best_rebuttal>
